utterances.text: If we can focus on what he did tell you, am I correct that your recollection of the meeting of May the 17th, wherein Mr. Markovic was present in Belgrade, he told you about an incident that he had just heard about - I believe in your notes it says "yesterday," so it would have been May the 16th - about how Arkan's men that had been sent to Kosovo were withdrawn after they killed an Albanian couple. Does that refresh your recollection as to where Rade Markovic deployed these persons that were said to be Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollection of the 17th of May is, in fact, quite fresh. It requires no effort on my part to remember. Rade Markovic said verbatim: "I heard yesterday that they," so he didn't say that they did that yesterday. He said that he had heard about it yesterday. He didn't specify the time when this incident happened or was caused by these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. But we are talking about the people, Arkan's men, being responsible for that incident, the killing of the Albanian couple, after which the -- they were withdrawn. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is your knowledge of this incident, this killing of the Albanian married couple, was it verified by the information you received from your security organs in the field?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not get any such information from the security organs in the field. This information I got from Rade Markovic at this meeting with Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you indicated earlier Kosovo Polje, but if I can direct your attention to Exhibit P2592, the extract from your diary, I believe you will see that your notes as to what Mr. Markovic said do not include a reference to Kosovo Polje for this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the English, which is not up on the screen yet. It's under the first paragraph where it says that -- at the end of that. There's a piece of information from yesterday that some of Arkan's men killed a married couple and are now under investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you see there, sir, that Mr. Markovic, at least according to your notes, did not mention the location where this had occurred?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is not mentioned here, but I made a presentation to President Milosevic and I told him that according to the information received from the security organs that there was a centre for Arkan's people, Arkan's men, in Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted)and then Rade Markovic made a comment. He confirms that they really are in Kosovo, but he does not make a mention of Kosovo Polje because I had already said that, having received this information from the security organs prior to the 17th of May meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So then you did get information from your security organs as to the location and the activities of the JSO and Arkan's men in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the initial information, there was no mention of JSO activity. There was a mention of various groups and then the wolves from Drina were mentioned and the people I had already mentioned. Among others, Arkan's men were mentioned in Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, either from your discussions with Mr. Markovic or from the information that you were receiving from your security organs in the field, did -- do you recall any further details, such as the identity of the perpetrators as JSO reservists or their names. For instance, Mr. Veselinovic or Mr. Todosijevic?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, or any of your security organs take steps to verify or follow up on the information, or did anyone ever report to you that the perpetrator of the shooting of the Albanian couple was convicted and sentenced to 40 years' imprisonment for war crimes by the Serbian judicial system?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This is the first time I hear of those names. I don't know what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, the only incident relating to the JSO or Arkan's men that you have identified thus far in your very lengthy testimony and statements is this one incident where an Albanian couple was murdered. Your security organs did not advise you of any such identical incidents, did they? And we're only talking about the one incident.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was another piece of information pertaining to the event of the 18th of April. It was stated that since it wasn't in the territory of Kosovo and was not encompassed by the indictment, it needed no explanation. But it also concerned that unit. Another thing I wanted to say, perhaps to cut your reference short, was that it wasn't for the military security organs to follow up and to see what the RDB and the MUP were doing in Kosovo. This was information learned along the way, but I focused on the information pertaining to army activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you be surprised to learn that there was an army -- that there was a soldier from the VJ involved in this incident? Did your security organs --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I inquire, Your Honour, which incident we're talking about. The witness has been talking about he heard from Rade Markovic about Arkan's men killing an Albanian couple sometime before the 17th of May. He learned the information the day before but there's no date referred to. Mr. Ivetic is talking about an Albanian couple that were killed by JSO. I'm not sure it's the same people, and I think from all the evidence in this case it's clear that there were more than one Albanian couple killed in early 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm talking about the one reported instance of JSO reservists from May the 16th of 1999; that is to say, the day before the meeting of which I have the exhibit 6D139, which are the documents relating to the arrest and detention of these JSO reservists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And this murder that you are referring to, was that in the area of Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Kosovska Mitrovica. That was going to be my next area of questioning, to see whether the recollection of the witness is perhaps inaccurate, since there's only this one instance that he heard about and the towns are slightly different names. And that's why I asked him that there was only one instance of an Albanian couple being reported to have been killed by one of the RDB's units that he had information on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I don't see anything objectionable about the question you asked, so please ask it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you be surprised to learn that there was a soldier from the VJ involved in the incident on May the -- in May in Kosovska Mitrovica wherein Mr. Veselinovic and Mr. Todosijevic, reserve members of the RDB's JSO unit, killed not only the Albanian couple but also some Serb civilians when they fled the scene?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already stated I don't know anything about that incident and I can't say anything. I only conveyed what Rade Markovic said when commenting on that piece of information, that in Kosovo Polje there was a centre for Arkan's men. This thing you with talking about is something I am unfamiliar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, you've referenced this killing and you've testified about it now in this proceeding and in your statement, and you referred to it in your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor as well. Is it your position that this killing by the -- this killing of the Albanian couple, was it by anyone's orders or was it a private criminal act, based on the information you have?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said what I know. It concerns Rade Markovic's words at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But you also indicated that you received information from your security organs in the field. I'd like to know if the information that you received from the security organs in the field gave the whole picture of what happened; and if so, what that picture was. So again I ask you: Did you have information that the killing was ordered by superiors or that it was an individual, personal, criminal act?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with that event. To reiterate, we need to separate between two things. One is the data held by the security organs when speaking in general about the paramilitary groups in Kosovo. It was said that, among others, Arkan's men were in a certain MUP centre in Kosovo Polje. This was a general assessment of the security organs before the 16th of May. Secondly, Rade Markovic commented by saying that not that yesterday the couple had been murdered, but that yesterday he found out they had been murdered. I don't know when they were killed or whether at all they were killed. It came from him. It wasn't up to the security organs to investigate. If that incident had been reported, you should look it up with the judicial organs which undertook the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'd like to find out what type of information you received from the field. Was all your information very general in nature, or did you actually get specific information? And I think the only way I can try and see that is by asking to look at a portion of Exhibit 6D139; in particular, I would like to turn to the third page of that exhibit which should be in English and in B/C/S since we did -- we were able to obtain an official translation. And, again, this is the -- this is the criminal charges filed relating to the arrest of these two JSO -- these two JSO -- and I see we've got a problem here. They're both in B/C/S. The English translation should start -- should start with the number 6D03-0693, according to the hard copy that I have. It should be -- we're pulling it up on our private e-court screen. Maybe I can go on and perhaps read the portion of it, so that we don't wait too long?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please do that, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, this is the information pertaining to the criminal charges filed in the arrest on the 16th of May, 1999, of Goran Veselinovic and Dragan Todosijevic, who according to the description of crimes at page 3, this is the -- yeah, this is the B/C/S version of page 3, where it says [B/C/S spoken], where it indicates that these individuals, along with their colleagues, that at least Mr. Veselinovic had been drinking at a tavern for four hours and with him was an army conscript dressed in full uniform with a red army beret, who actually is the one who suggested that the defendants go to -- go to his neighbours', his Albanian neighbours' over a personal dispute and scare them; and then the document goes on to explain the events that led up to the shooting and killing. And I would like to ask you, sir, did the information that you received from the field from your security organs, would it have included events where an army individual, army personnel, along with reservists of the RDB, the JSO, committed a crime, indeed the crime of murder, after getting drunk and going out with their weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained that the security organs were not the only ones obliged to react. If the incident took place as described here, I presume the MUP forwarded such information to the Pristina Corps command and that the judiciary was informed. Security organs are not informed on each and every incident happening in the field. I am not claiming that this is the same incident referred to by Rade Markovic. All I did was convey verbatim what he said at the meeting and why. I said that because it followed my presentation when I stated that I was in possession of some information that among other volunteer groups there were Arkan's men. And then he said: "Yesterday, I heard." He didn't say: "Yesterday, they were killed." He said he ordered them to pull out and didn't mention any proceedings. I don't know whether it referred to the same incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But again, you, as the deputy head of the security administration for the VJ, can point to no other incident that was reported to you that specifically referenced some of Rade Markovic's subordinates killing an Albanian couple in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I told you what I had been briefed by the security organs. The case of Kosovo Polje was not mentioned any longer. I said that it was for the first time that I heard those names that a soldier was involved. I'm not disputing this, but my security organs did not brief me on that and they were not tasked with following what the MUP was doing. They learned this along the way in their operational gathering. As for me, I was interested in the events in the field pursuant to General Ojdanic's orders. I did not follow up the case in Kosovo Polje or any other for that matter, particularly if it involved the MUP. The judiciary was tasked with doing that, be it the military or the civilian ones -- the civilian bodies of the judiciary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, you testified that your security organs were not the only ones obliged to react. From this exhibit, we can see the MUP on its side did an investigation, arrested the ones submitted to have committed the crime, and submitted them to the prosecutor's office. And I am representing to you the eventual disposition of the case was a judgement against defendant, Veselinovic, for 40 years' imprisonment. What else could the MUP do in that circumstance, or did the MUP do everything it was duty-bound to do?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot provide an assessment here, certainly because I never completed the police academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me move on to things that you have testified that you do know. At paragraph 42 of statement, you claim that Arkan himself had official identification of the "former Yugoslav MUP," as well as a Serbian RDB identification card. Are we to understand your testimony to be that Arkan had ID cards, that is identification cards, from the federal Savezna MUP -- Savezni MUP and the Serbian RDB but not the RJB, the public security department?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It pertains to the state security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, is that information as to whether Arkan had identification cards from the federal and the Serbian RDB, is that from the time-period of 1998 through 1999 or from the earlier period when you were the head of the UB, the Vojna Bezbednost, organ?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it pertains to both periods. I have no knowledge that in 1999 that ID was taken away from him [Realtime transcript read in error "me"]. I presume in 1999, he still had it with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever prepare a report on that; and if so, where can we find it?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why I would prepare a report. In the year 2000, some criminals were assassinated in Belgrade, and subsequently official RDB IDs of Montenegro were found on them. I see no reason for me to draft a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could I inquire of our Serbian speakers if that translation in line 11 on page 101, that that ID was taken away from me, as opposed to taken away from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It should have been him, from what I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 43 of your statement, you state that the MUP was "practically" under the control of Milosevic; yet, in the remainder of the paragraph, you only talk about your knowledge of the RDB and how it was turned into an untouchable institution above all others by Milosevic. Can I take from that the conclusions set forth in this paragraph are based entirely on your belief and understanding of how the RDB was set up and functioned and does not include the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think both sectors were under Milosevic's control, immediate control. The control over the RDB was particularly pronounced because it was supposed to have been subordinated to the Ministry of the Interior. In 1998, after some shuffle of positions, the RDB asked to be directly resubordinated to Milosevic and not to have to go through the Minister of the Interior. However, both sectors were objectively under Milosevic's control.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But you have no concrete facts to point to relating to the RJB, and, indeed, you've already stated several times that you did not attend the police academy or know the structure of the RJB.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. What are the facts that I have to corroborate that? In my logic, on the 17th of May, when the crime cases were discussed and when military commanders were present as well as people from the security service, in my view at that meeting President Milutinovic should have been there because the MUP was subordinated to him. He wasn't at that meeting and I never saw him at any other meeting. Vlajko Stojiljkovic was in the Republic of Serbia, the president of which was Mr. Milutinovic. Milutinovic was absent as if he were non-existent. There were no MUP representatives; there was no Minister of the Interior --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, we'll get to that meeting in a second. But what I'm trying to clarify is that essentially your conclusions as to the command structure of the RJB are based upon your speculation and inferences that you draw from who was present at a meeting and who wasn't present at a meeting. Is that a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it is. I do not try to speculate. I am quite convinced about the things I stated. If I'm uncertain about something, I mention that. I don't see why it would be disputable why no one from the MUP was present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You've never seen any official acts of the government or of the ministry describing or setting forth the command structure and operations of the RJB, have you? You're relying upon what you saw and what, in your gut, you believed that meant, which is speculation. Wouldn't you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Tell me specifically what was that speculation on my part that proved erroneous.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, I think it's rather clear for the questions that I ask, and it's not for me to answer your questions here today. I would like to ask some concrete questions to see how well you know the structure of the RJB, and I'm going to focus for my purposes on the MUP staff in Pristina. Am I correct that you actually have no concrete knowledge of how the MUP staff in Pristina was formed or how it functioned. You've never seen any official acts, declarations, or legislation in that regard?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't convey any factual information, since you're telling me I was speculating. I didn't even go there. I didn't mention it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you didn't mention it because you wouldn't have anything to say, correct? You don't know anything about the MUP staff in Pristina; that's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't necessary for me to know about the MUP headquarters. I wasn't there. I don't know where it was. I merely stated what I knew and what I saw on the 1st of June meeting. I said who was there and that's it. I never testified about anything else, and there was no speculation on my part. I stated the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to move on to another unrelated topic, unrelated to the MUP staff in Pristina. I'd like to talk about in your statement at paragraph 38, for instance, you mention the Skorpions and Boca Medic. Now, in paragraph 38 of your statement and in your testimony relating to the May 17th meeting with Milosevic, you have identified a murder of civilians by the Skorpions who were deployed as part of the SAJ, the "Specijalne Antiteroristicke Jedinice," in Podujevo. Now, the information that you received from your security operatives relating to this event, did it include the fact that the perpetrators of the killing were immediately withdrawn from Kosovo and reprimanded?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that they were pulled out of Podujevo. I have no information about them being punished in any way. As far as I know, the incident was processed only after 2000, first in Prokuplje and then the case was transferred to the Belgrade court. During some of the checks we ran, we established that they were again in Kosovo and that they returned some two to three days ago, and that information dates back to the 12th of May, again through security organs in Novi Sad. According to that, around the 8th or 9th of May, they returned from Kosovo and that they went there for the second time. Whether they were returned to the area of Novi Sad from Prolom Banja or they stayed at Prolom Banja for a while and then upon Trajkovic's [Realtime transcript read in error "Dragovic's"] request they were returned to Kosovo, I don't know. But we know that they were there twice and they returned there for the last time on the 8th or the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sure it will be corrected. At page 105, line 8, it says, "Dragovic's request." I believe the witness said, "Trajkovic's request."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, while we're at it. At line 3 I have some question and they returned some two to three days ago, and I'm sure that can't be right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I chose to read it as two to three days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately I was only plugged into the English on that occasion, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not referring to now; it's referring to the time of these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I have two questions for you relative to this. First of all, the perpetrators of the -- the perpetrators of the shooting in Podujevo, they -- based upon the information you had from the security organs, these individuals who were eventually sentenced to 20 years in prison were not acting on the orders of any of their superior officers, but rather were engaged again in a private criminal act. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the details. Most probably that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you indicated that they returned to Kosovo. I take it from the fact that in your, again, lengthy testimony, lengthy statement, lengthy interview with the OTP, that insofar as no other incidents were cited pertaining to this group, that you have no explicit information that they committed any crime if and when they were redeployed in Kosovo following Podujevo; otherwise, you would have mentioned it. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we can move on. At paragraph 68 of your statement and during your testimony the other day, you talked about how the Skorpions and Mr. Medic were discussed at the May 17th meeting, where Milosevic said that Stojiljkovic and Djordjevic needed to be told their heads wouldn't roll, but that Medic had to answer for the crimes. Was it your understanding that Milosevic's reference to heads not rolling was directed at Minister of the Interior Stojiljkovic and Assistant Minister of the Interior Djordjevic personally, that that comment was directed towards them?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, it was directed towards them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And was it your understanding and consensus from participating in this meeting that Stojiljkovic and Djordjevic were the MUP personnel that were responsible for Medic's group being in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speak about the Minister of the Interior, but specifically what Rade Markovic mentioned, that is, that he was informed by Djordjevic that it's correct that the group had been at Kosovo and that he ordered them to come back, it follows from this that he was responsible for collecting them, gathering them, together and sending them to Kosovo. Let me remind you of part of General Pavkovic's short conversation with Slobodan Medic, who said that Djordjevic was always getting them together and sending them where it was most difficult. and the same applies to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as far as this meeting and this group was concerned, I believe that you testified that your source for this information was your operative, Mr. Djurovic. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did Djurovic at that time, when you met with him, I believe -- or when you talked with him in May of 1999, when he told you about the Skorpions, at that time he didn't give you any additional information about any other crimes alleged against other MUP units, did he?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was an error in briefing because he did not come in order to brief on the situation in Kosovo, but to talk about problems concerning Jugoslav Petrusic's group, finding out what way they had arrived in Kosovo and where they were in Kosovo. When I asked him what else was happening, he mentioned paragroups and said that there was a group of Slobodan --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- who had committed a crime in Kosovo and that they had been sent to Kosovo again, and that was the information he gave me. And later on this was confirmed to me when I was in Kosovo again with General Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, I'm going to have to ask you to repeat the name that you had at the beginning of your answer because the interpreters did not catch the name apparently, and so it's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it refers to the then-Lieutenant-Colonel Djurovic, it concerns him. I don't know that I mentioned any other names.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The individual who had committed the crime, who was the -- affiliated with this group.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who specifically committed the crime, but it was a group under the command of Slobodan Medic, also known as Boca.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at that time that Lieutenant-Colonel Djurovic mentioned this to you, they didn't talk about this group as being Skorpions, did they? The name Skorpion was not utilised at that time, was it?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did mention the Skorpion group.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then, based on that, we checked who was in the group, where it was, whether it was still in Kosovo, and we gave that task to the security organs in Novi Sad. From them, we received information on this on the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I take it he did not mention any of the OPG at that time, did he, in May of 1999?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In May there was such information; but when Djurovic was there, he did not mention the OPG. It was the operative of the 52nd Rocket Brigade in Djakovica who gave the most information about 52 and the security organ in the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn -- if we can turn again to this May 17th, 1999, meeting for a few specific questions. First of all, you indicated that he was not -- that he was there to talk about the Petrusic group. Am I correct that the VJ volunteer group led by Jugoslav Petrusic, the so-called Pauk, P-a-u-k, saboteurs, was the central theme and main topic on the agenda of the meeting with Milosevic on May 17th, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was not a separate topic. The Pauk group was not a separate topic. The main topic, or rather, when Colonel Djurovic came at our invitation to Belgrade on the 8th of May, and he remained there on the 9th of May. When Gajic and I were interested in what else was happening in Kosovo and asked him about that, then he gave us information about the Skorpions. When we from the army were briefing President Milosevic, we mentioned, among other things, that we had dealt with that group because that group had already been arrested before the meeting; not the entire group but Petrusic and Orasanin, two persons, their commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when we're talking about Petrusic and Orasanin, am I also -- am I correct that the RDB, the State Security Service, was the initial source of information about Petrusic and his group that ultimately led to the concerns and to the actions that your organs took to arrest these individuals?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the State Security Service did not deliver this information to the military security service, rather, it informed Milosevic of this; and then Milosevic told General Geza about it. This shows what kind of cooperation the MUP had with the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again you say "MUP," but we're really talking about the RDB, not the rest of the MUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, given the RDB's involvement in uncovering this Petrusic's group, isn't that an altogether logical reason why the RDB's chief, the assistant minister, General Markovic, would be the one present from the MUP for this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the reasons were for him to be there. I'm more surprised by the reasons why the other people from the public security weren't there, because the main topic concerned indicia about war crimes in Kosovo. The topic was not the Pauk group, for which the state security and military security were responsible, but crimes in Kosovo. That's why the most responsible generals from the army were there and also those in charge of the security services, such as Mr. Ojdanic and Mr. Pavkovic. Had this been a professional meeting of the state security and military security, Mr. Pavkovic and Mr. Ojdanic would not have attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you claim in your written statement that the day before this meeting, that is to say on May the 16th, 1999, General Pavkovic had complained that General Lukic had refused to participate in a Joint Commission with the VJ to investigate bodies of victims found on the terrain to ascertain what had happened. Do you recall whether it was discussed at the May 17th meeting with Milosevic at all; and if so, why is there no reference to such statements in your notes of this meeting, again Exhibit P2592?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that I did not write down what was said at that meeting by General Pavkovic. He had a briefing in writing which he put forward. Later on, when I was writing down what had happened at the meeting, there's a place where General Pavkovic draws attention to the poor cooperation with the MUP on the ground; and then Milosevic transformed this into a separate topic. He said that anyone who was hindering this cooperation was committing sabotage and so on. So there is a part where General Pavkovic talks of the poor cooperation between both MUPs. The fact that there was evasion of -- that there were attempts to evade the forming of such a commission, General Djurovic spoke about this, and that's why the army formed its own commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is: At that meeting, the Milosevic meeting of May the 17th, 1999, did General Pavkovic explicitly reference General Sreten Lukic as being someone who had been refusing and rejecting to participate and cooperate in such a Joint Commission? Did he explicit reference General Sreten Lukic in that capacity?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he mentioned him explicitly. He just mentioned the MUP. He mentioned him explicitly on the 16th of May when briefing General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, see, sir, the problem that I have is your notes obviously don't have a reference to it, because now you say that he didn't reference Mr. Lukic at that meeting. But more curiously I have been unable to find in your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor that you ever mentioned General Lukic in that capacity until this statement that was done a couple weeks ago. When is it that you refreshed your recollection to remember that General Lukic was explicitly referenced, and what jogged your memory?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't that something jogged my memory. I have it written down in my notebook. In my diary as you call it, I wrote down the contents of the meeting of the 16th of May. And when preparing to testify, when Kosovo was at issue, I went through my notebook; and when making a statement on Kosovo alone, I put forward what happened on the 16th of May. When testifying in the Milosevic case, I did not put forward such a detailed account of that meeting, but it is in my notebook. And I believe that other generals, especially General Gajic, who attended the meeting would tell you the same, because he and I were known for writing a lot at meetings, taking lots of notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, where is the reference to Mr. Lukic by Pavkovic in this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour. I have it coming in at paragraph 62 on my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm too far ahead, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On my version, it's page 17 in the middle, where they're talking. It says, "Pavkovic told Ojdanic that he had asked General Lukic that they form a" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, first of all, Mr. Vasiljevic, did you -- did you have your notebook with you during the multiple days that the OTP interviewed you in 2002, I believe?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't bring my notebooks to those interviews. But when I was preparing for the interviews, I made use of my notebooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you give those notebooks to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you still have them?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did your information, that is to say either from security organs in the field or from any other source, any other generals, for instance, did any of that information advise you of the fact that prior to your meeting in May, specifically on May the 2nd, 1999, there indeed was a joint meeting at the command of the Pristina Corps between the top officials of the MUP and the VJ, specifically relating to joint work to investigate, document, and determine what was the cause or what was the responsibility of various instances where there had been unidentified bodies found in the terrain to determine the zone of responsibility ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- to determine the facts so that those events could be properly investigated. Did you have knowledge of such a meeting from May the 2nd, 1999, that resulted in communiques from both --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Surely this question must come to an end --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm happy to have it be answered now if he has information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about any such meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know of any communique issued thereafter by the MUP staff in Pristina, initiating a request for joint work in cooperation with the VJ, specifically for some unidentified bodies that had been discovered on the terrain?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Apart from the information I gave at the closed part of the session, I had no other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as far as the MUP of the Republic of Serbia is concerned, do you know or did you have information from your security organs or from any other source that from the 24th of March, 1999, through the 20th of June, 1999, the MUP organs filed official criminal charges against various persons for crimes that were suspected of having been committed, including approximately 629 civilian persons, 86 approximately members of the MUP of Serbia, approximately 112 members of the army, and I believe over a thousand unknown perpetrators. Are you aware of that effort at investigation and documentation and processing?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware only of what I said. The Minister of the Interior, Vlajko Stojiljkovic, said at the joint meeting with the MUP at the Army of Yugoslavia in July; that is, that they had 16 cases that had been processed and dealt with. I don't have the information that you have just given and he did not give it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the other day with respect to those 16 you indicated that it was your belief at the time that those were just the more serious crimes and incidents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's impossible that there was only such a small number of cases in total in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The numbers I've just quoted to you are much more realistic, are they not?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They might be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I have just -- I have a couple questions relating to an exhibit that came in, in part through your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if I could have clarification, It's my understanding that P1898, that's the handwritten purported diary of Obrad Stevanovic, that just the one portion that's referenced in the one paragraph of the witness's statement has been introduced into evidence and, therefore, I will not be opening the Pandora's box by questioning him on just that one aspect, which is what I tend to do with that one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. That is one of the documents that perhaps Mr. Hannis will apply to have admitted in general. I'm not sure. Is that one likely to be the subject of your application?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: A larger portion of the diary, anyhow, rather than that one specific passage may be offered to place it in context and in time, because there's an issue I think about what date those notes refer to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But only in relation to the matter raised in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So that one paragraph. Thank you, Your Honour, I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, this exhibit, this handwritten diary came up in connection with your testimony relative to the May 17th meeting. The other day you testified that you followed the testimony of General Obrad Stevanovic during the Milosevic trial, and you wanted to comment on his sworn testimony that the reference to no body, no crime was actually relating to information received from the military security organs about the activities of the KLA. Now, I don't mean to test your memory, but I have gone back and checked the transcript of Mr. Stevanovic's testimony. And what you recalled him as testifying to is inaccurate. At page 40382, lines 3 through 10 of the Milosevic transcript, Mr. Stevanovic testified under oath: "I think I have explained this during my interview in Belgrade. At that meeting, I don't know precisely which meeting that was, but I do have a vague memory. One of the representatives of the security forces, whether it was the military or the civilian security, I don't know, warned against perfidious actions by terrorists; namely, that they are removing the corpses of their victims and the casualties of anti-terrorist actions, only to gather them again and place them in mass graves in order to blame those mass graves on Serbian forces." Now, sir, you had earlier refuted that this information could have come from military security. Now, I take it, being refreshed with the actual testimony of Mr. Stevanovic, where he says: "I don't know whether it's state or military security," you cannot exclude that state security, the RDB, may have provided that type of information to him, can you? You could only speak for your organ, correct, your security organ?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Quoting this passage, you did not mention what was concluded before that, i.e., that the military service was doing a perfidious job, that they wanted to prove NATO right in starting the air-strikes. So it was the military service that provided this information, and it was being criticised for having given this information to President Milosevic on the 17th of May. You have extracted only this passage, which I did not deny, but it refers to the previous passage that it's the military service that is doing a perfidious job.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we could seek to have the transcript portion put into evidence if Your Honours feel it necessary. I did not have it prepared in e-court today, but I think the transcript will speak for itself. I'm not here to weigh one person over the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I assume you've quoted it accurately and that should be sufficient for our purposes. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That portion, yes, Your Honour, but I think you may need more than that portion because the question is discussed for some length of time back and forth between Mr. Nice and Mr. Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you can deal with that in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: By the way, Mr. Vasiljevic, the notebook that you saw, that was only shown to you after you testified in the Milosevic case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And who showed it to you? Was it the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And that was shown to you after Mr. Stevanovic had completed his testimony in June of 2005. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the notebook you refer to there, Mr. Ivetic? Is that the Stevanovic diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The Stevanovic diary, correct, the P1898.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to focus just a handful of questions on the operative sweep groups again. First of all, I would like to ask you if you are aware when the operative sweep groups were first established within the structure of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you be surprised to learn that the official act of the government as far back as 1970 established these operative sweep groups, in response to the well-publicised infiltration of the Radusa terrorist cell in Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether an order about the formation of those groups was in place, and I'm not sure about the exact name of those groups. I don't know whether it was in force at the time when the SFRY ceased to exist when the FRY began existing. I don't know whether that practice dates back to the 1970s. I think it was actually 1972, and I don't know whether it remained in force until 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And these are very small anti-terrorist groups, these operative sweep groups, that you recall from 1972. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no separate formations. They comprised MUP personnel. Tactically speaking, groups to cover certain areas were formed, and such groups always were of mixed composition. They comprised military -- the military police, the Territorial Defence elements, and some other elements in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That was not a part of the MUP establishment in 1972; it was merely to address a situation in the field which called for such a unit. Such groups were formed in the specific areas in which there was information on the existence of certain terrorist groups. Not every area had an operational sweep group, and it was a long time ago, back in 1972.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, based on your knowledge, sir, isn't it a fact that the same principles were employed in 1998 and 1999 as well with these smaller groups for specific purposes?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that. But in 1972, you didn't have groups paring their names such as Legija, Magla, and Sigma, and so on and so forth. They were not formed as separate units with their name or designation. I did not question the need for such a thing back in 1999 to have something at a tactical level to join the MUP and the army in order to clear the terrain, a certain part of the land. As for why some were called operational sweep groups, whereas others had different functions to go from one house to the next and expel Albanians, this has got nothing to do with some operational sweep groups dating back to 1972.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen any formal written act or declaration relative to the formation, command, organisation of either the PJP, the "Posebne Jedinice Policije," or the OPG units?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see such information. I was only briefed orally to the extent I required.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that your source for information about the OPG and the PJP comes exclusively from persons that were not members of these units and, in fact, were not members of the MUP of Serbia, i.e., your information comes from third parties?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what party it came from, but it came from the security organs for sure. And I would call that first-hand or first-party information, and they received that information directly as well. Therefore, it is not a third-party or third-hand information. I conveyed directly what was told to me in the field by the security organs. I didn't see any such documents, and I have no official information by the MUP -- from the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, where are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the OPG groups which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed, but how close are we --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To finishing? I've got I'd say probably another 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. I think we should interrupt at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That concludes our hearing for today, Mr. Vasiljevic. I'm fairly confident, barring unforeseen events, that tomorrow will be your last day with us. I won't be held to that, but it's as good an indication as I can give you. So please return ready to resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Meanwhile, you may leave with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will now go into private session to deal with a matter which affects the personal security of an individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
